gloss: to fall asleep; to go to sleep

definitions.gloss: to fall asleep; to go to sleep
definitions.explanation: A somewhat literary or gentle expression for falling asleep. More elegant than simply {寝|ね}る, often used in narrative, bedtime contexts, or when describing someone drifting off peacefully.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{眠|ねむ}りについた。
{温|あたた}かい{布団|ふとん}の{中|なか}で{眠|ねむ}りにつく。
examples.english: To fall asleep in a warm futon.

examples.japanese: {昨夜|ゆうべ}はなかなか{眠|ねむ}りにつけなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't fall asleep last night.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れていたので、{横|よこ}になるとすぐに{眠|ねむ}りについた。
examples.english: I was tired, so I fell asleep as soon as I lay down.

notes:
Composed of {眠|ねむ}り (sleep, as a noun) + に (particle) + つく (to settle into). Literally "to settle into sleep." The verb つく conjugates normally: {眠|ねむ}りについた (past), {眠|ねむ}りにつける (potential), {眠|ねむ}りにつけない (negative potential).

More refined than {寝|ね}る, which is the everyday word for sleeping or going to bed. {眠|ねむ}りにつく focuses specifically on the transition into sleep and has a softer, more literary tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- すぐに{眠|ねむ}りにつく: to fall asleep right away
- なかなか{眠|ねむ}りにつけない: to have trouble falling asleep
- {深|ふか}い{眠|ねむ}りにつく: to fall into a deep sleep
- {静|しず}かに{眠|ねむ}りにつく: to fall asleep quietly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寝|ね}る: to sleep; to go to bed — the basic everyday word
- {寝|ね}つく: to fall asleep — similar meaning but more colloquial
- {眠|ねむ}る: to sleep — focuses on the state of being asleep rather than the transition
